question.text: A gas mixture consists of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> moles of oxygen and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> moles of argon at temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math>. Neglecting all vibrational modes we calculated the total internal energy of the system to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>T</mi></math>. What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>?

solution.text:
The internal energy of n moles of a gas is U=12nFRT
where F = number of degrees of freedom.
The internal energy of 2 moles of oxygen at temperature T is

U1=12×2×5RT=5RT    (F = 5 for oxygen molecule)

The total internal energy of 4 moles of argon at temperature T is

    U2=12×4×3RT=6RT (F = 3 for argon molecule)

Total internal energy =U1+U2=11RT

⇒x=11
